justification.rationale: No experimental APIs are used at all, so nothing is gratuitous; the app deliberately stays on the stable Nuxt 4 line and even avoids vue-router 5.4's new experimental definePage/query-param features, which would have been tempting for its URL-heavy filters.

findings.issue: vue 3.5.44 and vue-router 5.4.0 are declared as exact-pinned direct dependencies; Nuxt 4.6.3 already declares vue ^3.5.44 and vue-router ^5.4.0, so the pins are redundant and can silently drift from what a future Nuxt version requires.
findings.suggestion: Drop vue and vue-router from dependencies and let Nuxt manage them, or keep ranges identical to Nuxt's (^3.5.44 / ^5.4.0).

findings.issue: nuxt is exact-pinned to 4.6.3, a patch released 2026-10-27 containing security fixes (e.g. GHSA-9v7c-q64q-vv33); an exact pin means future security patches in 4.6.x will not be picked up on a fresh install.
findings.suggestion: Prefer a caret range such as ^4.6.3 (or a lockfile-based update policy) so patch-level security fixes are picked up automatically.

summary: This app is essentially zero-experimental: no experimental flags, no unstable_* names, no preview/RC/canary APIs, and every composable and server handler it touches (useAsyncData, useFetch with query/watch, useHead, defineEventHandler, getRouterParam, setResponseStatus) is long-stable Nuxt 4 / Nitro surface. It rides the current stable release (nuxt 4.6.3, published 2026-10-27) with vue and vue-router pinned to exactly the versions Nuxt itself requires, and notably declines vue-router 5.4's new experimental definePage/query-param APIs and Nuxt 5's preview channel. The only notes are dependency-hygiene: redundant exact pins of vue/vue-router that could drift on upgrade, and an exact nuxt pin that suppresses future patch-level security fixes.
